title: About the AAIA exam
description: What the Advanced in AI Audit (AAIA) exam from ISACA® looks like, who can take it, how to book it, what happens on the day and after, and how passing turns into certification. AI means artificial intelligence. Written in plain language by KaiSip from ISACA's published information.
disclaimer: KaiSip is an independent study app. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by ISACA®. AAIA is a trademark of ISACA, used here only to describe the exam. CISA® is a registered trademark of ISACA. Other credentials named on this page belong to their owners. ISACA alone sets the exam rules and decides eligibility and certification. No study app can promise a pass, including this one.
check_before_booking: Fees, rules and requirements on this page were checked on the date shown. They can change, so check isaca.org before you book.

sections.title: The exam at a glance
sections.summary: A 150-minute (2.5-hour), computer-based exam of 90 multiple-choice questions, scored on a scale from 200 to 800. A score of 450 or higher passes.
items: 90 multiple-choice questions in 150 minutes. Each question has four options and one best answer.
It is written for working auditors: ISACA requires an active credential from its Qualified Prerequisite List, such as the Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA). The next section lists them.
Scores are scaled from 200 (the lowest) to 800 (every scored question answered correctly). You pass with 450 or more.
Scaling keeps different versions of the exam comparable, so 450 is not a fixed percentage of questions.
Some questions are unscored pre-test items, and ISACA does not say how many. Treat every question as if it counts.
There is no penalty for a wrong answer, so answer every question.
Your results include a breakdown by domain. It is for your information only; your score counts total correct answers, whatever the domain.
Languages: English, Simplified Chinese and Spanish.
You take it on a computer, either at a PSI test center or online with a remote proctor from PSI. Residents of India, Mainland China and Hong Kong can take it only at a test center.
The current content outline is ISACA's AAIA Examination Content Outline, dated June 2025.
KaiSip's practice and mock scores are not scaled exam scores. Use them to find gaps, not to predict a result.

sections.title: Who qualifies
sections.summary: AAIA builds on an audit or accounting credential you already hold. ISACA names the qualifying credentials in its Qualified Prerequisite List, and the credential must stay active.
items: Every holder of the Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA) credential qualifies.
Holders of the credentials below qualify if they work in an IT audit or IT advisory role. Check with ISACA how to show that role when you apply.
Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) from the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA), and US Certified Public Accountant (CPA) from a US state board of accountancy.
Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA): Chartered Certified Accountant or Fellow (FCCA).
CPA Australia: Certified Practicing Accountant (CPA) or Fellow (FCPA). Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CA ANZ): Chartered Accountant (CA) or Fellow (FCA).

Japanese CPA from the Japan Financial Services Agency, Canadian Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) from the provincial accounting bodies, and Hong Kong CPA or FCPA from the Hong Kong Institute of CPAs (HKICPA).
Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales (ICAEW): Associate (ACA) or Fellow (FCA). Certified National Accountant (CNA) from the Association of National Accountants of Nigeria (ANAN).
Because every candidate already holds an audit or accounting credential, KaiSip's course focuses on applying audit ideas to AI rather than on audit basics.

sources.label: ISACA AAIA Exam Candidate Guide, Certification

sections.title: The three domains and their weights
sections.summary: ISACA's June 2025 content outline splits the exam into three domains. A domain's weight is its share of the exam, so it is a good guide to where your study time goes.
items: Domain 2 alone is close to half the exam, so it usually earns the most practice time; let your weakest areas, weighed by their share, decide the rest.
Domain 1 settles who owns each AI decision and risk. Its ideas of ownership, policy and inventory show up in every domain.
Domain 3 is the smallest at 21%, yet about one question in five still comes from it: auditing AI and using AI in the audit.

Read every question as the IS (information systems) auditor unless it tells you otherwise. You assess, recommend and report; the model owner, senior management, the AI governance committee and the board decide.
When you practice, look for the AI-specific fact that decides the answer, such as a retrained model, a vendor's model update or a reviewer who approves without real review (automation bias).

sources.label: ISACA AAIA Exam Candidate Guide, Appendix

sections.title: Registering and fees
sections.summary: You register and pay through your ISACA account, then book a date with PSI. You have 6 months from registering to sit the exam.
steps: Check that you hold a qualifying credential, and that a PSI test center near you has dates or your device passes the online compatibility check.
Create or log in to your ISACA account. Use your name exactly as it appears on the ID you will bring on exam day.
Register for the exam and pay. Registration is open all year, and your 6-month eligibility period starts on the day you register.
Starting 48 hours after you pay, book your date with PSI through your ISACA account. Appointments open up to 90 days ahead.
items: Exam fee: US$459 for ISACA members, US$599 for non-members. Your price depends on whether you are a member when you register.
Fees are not refunded and cannot be transferred. If your 6 months end before you sit the exam, the fee is lost.
One part of ISACA's guide describes one 6-month extension for US$75, while another says no extensions are allowed. Plan to sit within 6 months, and ask ISACA support before relying on an extension.
Reschedule for free at least 48 hours before your appointment. Within 48 hours, you either sit the exam or lose the fee.
Changing your exam language means rescheduling, so make that change at least 48 hours ahead too.
If you miss your appointment or arrive more than 15 minutes late, you also lose the fee.

For a genuine hardship, such as sudden illness, a death in your immediate family or a traffic accident, contact PSI within 72 hours after the missed appointment, with documents. If PSI declines, you register and pay again.
Need special testing accommodations? Request them while you register, with a form completed with your health care professional, at least 4 weeks before your preferred date.

sources.label: ISACA AAIA Exam Candidate Guide, Section II

sections.title: Test center or online
sections.summary: You can take it at a PSI test center or online with a remote proctor. Residents of India, Mainland China and Hong Kong must use a test center. Follow ISACA's guide and your check-in specialist; ask ISACA support if unsure.
items: Test center: find the address, plan your route and arrive at least 30 minutes early. Lockers or a set area hold your belongings, and you may share the room with other candidates.

Online: run the compatibility check on the computer and network you will actually use. ISACA recommends a personal computer: an employer's firewall can block PSI's software, and if a work computer fails on exam day, you retake at your own expense.

Read ISACA's Remote Proctoring Guide before an online exam. It suggests trying PSI's tutorial test first (about 30 minutes, up to three tries), and you can start check-in up to 30 minutes before your appointment.
Clear your workspace completely, use one monitor and keep facing the screen for the whole exam.
Check-in includes a 360-degree room scan, a desk scan and a floor-to-ceiling scan, then a mirror check showing your screen, your keyboard and all four edges of the screen.
You can scan with an external webcam, your laptop camera and a mirror, or your phone through a QR code. Move the phone out of the testing area once the scan is done.
Chat with the remote proctor is in English only.
Online, you may not use a phone, read questions aloud, take notes, eat or drink, walk around, have anyone pass through or open other programs. Breaking these rules voids the exam and the fee.

sources.label: ISACA AAIA Exam Candidate Guide, Section III

sections.title: Exam day
sections.summary: Bring one valid ID, arrive or log in early, and leave everything else behind. AAIA allows one short break, and the clock keeps running.
items: Bring one current, original, government-issued ID showing your name, photo and signature, such as a passport, driver's license or national identity card. Copies and handwritten IDs are not accepted.
Your first and last name must match your registration; a middle name is not needed. Without valid ID you cannot sit the exam, and you lose the fee.
Test center: arrive at least 30 minutes early. More than 15 minutes late counts as a missed appointment, and the fee is lost.
Nothing comes in with you: no notes or paper, calculator, phone, smartwatch, smart glasses, headphones, earbuds or bag, and no food or drink, not even water.
You may take one break of up to 10 minutes, with the proctor's permission. The exam clock keeps running.
A short tutorial runs before the exam starts. Read it closely; it covers how the exam screens work.
Pace: 150 minutes for 90 questions is 100 seconds a question. Aim for about 90 to leave time for flagged questions. Answer every one; a blank earns nothing.
You may not photograph any part of the exam, including the results screen, or share its content afterward.

sources.label: ISACA AAIA Exam Candidate Guide, Section III

sections.title: After the exam
sections.summary: A preliminary pass or fail shows on screen when you finish. The official result follows within 10 working days.
items: Your official score arrives by email and in your MyISACA account within 10 working days.
Results show your scaled score and how you did by domain. They do not show which questions you got wrong.
If you did not pass, you can ask for a rescore in writing through ISACA support within 30 days of your results. The fee is US$75.
Retakes: up to four attempts in the 12 months from your first. Wait 30 days before the second attempt, then 90 days before each later one. Each attempt costs the full fee.
Concerns about how the exam was run go to ISACA support within 48 hours of finishing.
If you pass, you cannot sit AAIA again during the 5 years you have to apply for certification (see the next section).
Passing is not the same as being certified. You still need to apply, as the next section explains.

sources.label: ISACA AAIA Exam Candidate Guide, Section IV

sections.title: Becoming and staying certified
sections.summary: After passing, you apply while your prerequisite credential is active, then keep AAIA current with yearly learning in AI and a fee. ISACA decides every application.
steps: Wait for your official score, then pay the one-time US$50 application processing fee.
Submit the AAIA application within 5 years of passing, while you hold an active credential from the Qualified Prerequisite List.
Agree to follow ISACA's Code of Professional Ethics, Terms of Use and Privacy Policy, its continuing professional education (CPE) policy and the Information Systems Auditing Standards.
items: Keeping AAIA: earn at least 10 CPE hours a year in AI, and 30 over each 3-year period, starting the calendar year after you certify.
AI CPE hours may also count toward your other ISACA certifications when they meet those requirements.
Keep the prerequisite credential you applied with active.
Annual maintenance fee: US$20 for members, US$35 for non-members, due by January 1.
ISACA audits a sample of CPE records, and not meeting the requirements can cost you the certification. Keep your CPE evidence.
